b: The Indie Film Site Network, of which Slant is a member, has named Hamaguchi Ryusuke’s All of a Sudden the winner of the 2026 IFSN Advocate Award, making it the first narrative feature to receive the honor. Established in 2022, the award recognizes independent films that illuminate a humanitarian issue with a singular artistic vision. The winner receives one million media impressions across the network’s sites: The Film Stage, Hammer to Nail, IONCINEMA.com, Next Best Picture, RogerEbert.com, and Slant.

Virginie Efira stars in All of a Sudden as Marie-Lou, a care worker in Paris who strikes up an unlikely friendship with Mari (Okamoto Tao), a theater director reckoning with a life-changing cancer diagnosis. In his review from the New York Film Festival, Slant’s Keith Uhlich wrote that the film’s positivity “still feels like a balm and is, in toto, more than earned.”

“Bringing a staggering level of humanity and insight to life’s mysteries throughout his career, Ryusuke Hamaguchi has delivered his most universally empathetic film yet with All of a Sudden,” said Jordan Raup, co-founder of IFSN and editor-in-chief and co-founder of The Film Stage. “Led by luminous performances from Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto, this drama embodies everything the ideal IFSN Advocate Award encompasses: living everyday life with humble compassion toward anyone you encounter. That Hamaguchi also eloquently dissects how modern-era capitalism is rotting out the globe is nothing short of a miracle.”

This year’s finalists, each of which will receive 100,000 media impressions, are Poh Si Teng’s American Doctor, Walter Thompson-Hernández’s If I Go Will They Miss Me, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s NAZA, Ross McElwee’s Remake, and Barbara Kopple’s Union Town. Prior winners include Julia Loktev’s My Undesirable Friends: Part I – Last Air in Moscow, Basel Adra, Hamdan Ballal, Yuval Abraham, and Rachel Szor’s Oscar-winning No Other Land, D. Smith’s Kokomo City, and Shaunak Sen’s All That Breathes.

All of a Sudden premiered at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, where Efira and Okamoto shared the best actress prize, and went on to win the Silver Hugo for best screenplay at the Chicago International Film Festival. It’s Japan’s official submission for the 2027 Academy Awards and is up for four Gotham Awards. Neon opens the film in theaters on November 25.
